# FDGD037

> NOT PERMITTED: Renaming a Method Parameter

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section D.11.1 Renaming a Method Parameter. Can cause: compilation break.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Status: verified

Breaks only callers that use named arguments, but the benefit of a rename is slight. PublicApiAnalyzers (optional in /fdg-setup) can flag changes to the public API.

## From the book

Renaming a method parameter can cause a compile-time break in languages, such as C#, that permit calling methods with named arguments.

Most callers don’t specify named parameter syntax for required parameters, so the risk of introducing a break is minimal; however, the benefit of renaming the parameter is slight. The .NET BCL team considers this an unacceptable breaking change.
